en: Death Valley holds the record for the highest air temperature ever recorded on Earth at 56.7 degrees Celsius.
Sand particles are the largest in soil, measuring between 0.05 and 2.0 millimeters in diameter.
Talc is the softest mineral on the Mohs hardness scale with a rating of one, while diamond is the hardest at ten.
About 97 percent of Earth's water is salty ocean water, leaving only three percent as fresh water.
Jupiter is so massive that more than 1,300 Earths could fit inside its total volume.
Proxima Centauri is the closest star to our solar system, located about 4.24 light-years away.
The Moon's diameter is about one-quarter the size of Earth's diameter, measuring roughly 3,474 kilometers across.
The 1991 Mount Pinatubo eruption injected 20 million tons of sulfur dioxide into the stratosphere, cooling the global climate.
The troposphere extends about eight kilometers above the poles and fifteen kilometers above the equator.
Gold is incredibly dense, weighing about 19 times more than an equal volume of water.
A single day on Venus lasts 243 Earth days, which is longer than its year of 225 Earth days.
The Pacific Ocean covers about 32 percent of Earth's total surface area, making it larger than all landmasses combined.
